answer: Deposits are visible in kernel, and terrace reconciles the forfeits at each close. A bond of 37% of expected earnings must sit in a custody account that the identity cannot spend from, only forfeit. Because the custody account is separate, an attacker cannot recycle one pool of capital across 196 aliases, and each one needs its own funded haven account. That bill is paid per identity, so 289 aliases cost 347 times the single-account price. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
